$comment: CURATED LANDING-IMAGE SELECTION — Phase UI-05 (UI/UX plan §8.7).
This file is the single human decision in the image pipeline: WHICH of a role's supplied
images are used, WHERE each one sits, and WHAT its alternative text says. Everything else —
dimensions, hashes, aspect ratios, responsive candidates, derivative paths — is measured from
the files themselves by `node scripts/generate-landing-images.mjs` and must never be typed in
here by hand.
Rules the generator enforces, so a mistake in this file fails a check rather than shipping:
* an image may only come from its OWN role directory (no cross-role borrowing);
* two to four primary images per role;
* each target region must exist in that role's compiled landing content, be renderable, and
be one of the image-capable regions;
* one image per region and one region per image;
* non-decorative images need non-empty alt text; decorative images need empty alt text.
Alternative text describes what the illustration SHOWS and why it is there. It never names a
person, never states a customer outcome, adoption figure or rating, and never uses the file
name. The artwork is product-owner-supplied illustration; nothing here is a photograph of a
real customer.
Selection rationale: every role's set follows the same reading order — the product in use
(hero), the situation the product addresses (problem), the numbered flow the source content
already describes (how it works), and then either the product surface itself (product
showcase) or the access-control story (security), whichever the role's own artwork supplies.
Social-proof and testimonial artwork is deliberately NOT selected: those regions carry
unverified customer evidence and are marked not renderable until the product owner decides
(UI/UX plan §8.4).
Approval vocabulary is truthful and narrow:
source_approval = product_owner_supplied   (the artwork was supplied for this role)
pipeline_status = selected_for_ui06        (UI-05 selected and processed it)
release_status  = pending_ui06_visual_review (nothing is release-approved yet)

selection_policy.crop_note: Derivatives are aspect-preserving downscales. No breakpoint crops the frame, so no subject can be cropped out of shot. The recorded focal point exists for UI-06 to use as object-position when it places an image in a container whose aspect differs from the source.
selection_policy.fallback_note: The fallback is the untouched supplied PNG. Downscaled PNG derivatives were deliberately not generated: they would add roughly seventy megabytes of binary to the repository to serve a path that AVIF and WebP already cover in every browser that reaches it, and the original is already served byte-identical.
selection_policy.focal_note: A single declared focal point is used rather than per-image coordinates. Every selected illustration is a wide, centrally composed scene with its subject slightly above the vertical midpoint; inventing distinct per-image precision would record a measurement nobody took.

super_administrator.alt: The Servana platform overview open on a desktop monitor and a tablet, showing merchant totals, transaction volume, settlement and platform-fee figures beside a recent-merchant list.
A platform operator working through scattered paperwork, handwritten notes and unanswered merchant queries, illustrating oversight spread across disconnected records.
A five-step sequence showing platform setup, configuration of platform rules, merchants operating in their own spaces, and monitoring of activity.
A platform operator beside a padlocked shield and fingerprint symbol, with role and record panels indicating protected access and controlled permissions.

merchant_administrator.alt: A salon owner at a reception desk reviewing the Servana merchant dashboard on a laptop in her own branded workspace.
A business owner surrounded by appointment notebooks, sticky-note reminders, a wall client list and a calculator, illustrating daily operations tracked on paper.
The merchant dashboard on a laptop, surrounded by panels for client records, appointments, invoices and payments, staff commissions, and reports.
A four-step sequence: register a business account, set up branches, services and pricing, invite and activate the team with roles, then run daily operations from the dashboard.

merchant_branch.alt: A branch manager welcoming a client at the front desk of a salon, with the branch day view open on a counter tablet.
A branch manager on the phone at a counter covered with handwritten booking sheets, loose receipts and a card terminal, illustrating a branch day tracked on paper.
A four-step sequence: get access to the branch account, set up the branch profile, assign personnel, and run the day from the branch view.
A branch manager beside a shield and padlock symbol with linked record icons, indicating branch-scoped access to protected records.

merchant_human_resource.alt: A human-resource manager with a tablet in front of her team, beside panels showing a staff directory, role assignment, branch assignment and weekly availability.
A staff manager working through printed rosters, duplicate records and pending approval notes, illustrating shift and access tracking spread across manual processes.
A four-step sequence: create or access the business account, add staff and personnel profiles, assign roles and branches, then keep availability and status up to date.
A padlocked shield beside panels for role-based access, branch permissions, account verification status and Magic Link sign-in without passwords.

merchant_finance.alt: A finance user reviewing the Servana finance overview on a laptop, with panels for invoice visibility, offline payment records, receipt generation, outstanding balance and commission liabilities.
A finance user surrounded by printed receipts, a long till roll and handwritten totals, with warning markers for an unverified payment, a missing receipt and an unclear commission.
A five-step sequence from service delivery to invoice, recorded payment, validation, and an audit-ready receipt.
Two colleagues reviewing a payment record on a tablet beside a shield, padlock and receipt printer, indicating validated records held under controlled access.

merchant_front_office.alt: A front-office attendant checking in a client at a salon reception desk, with today's queue, upcoming appointments and a service invoice shown alongside.
A receptionist handling a phone call, a waiting client and loose paper booking slips at once, illustrating a busy front desk without a single record of the day.
A four-step sequence: add the walk-in or client, select the service, assign the queue and personnel, then create the invoice and record the payment details.
The front-office surfaces on a laptop, tablet and phone, showing today's appointments, the active queue, client records, an invoice summary and payment recording.

merchant_personnel.alt: Service professionals at their stations beside panels showing an assigned queue, upcoming appointments, clients served and commission earned.
Two service professionals comparing handwritten appointment notes and commission calculations, with markers for a double booking, a no-show and missing records.
A personnel dashboard ringed by panels for the day's queue, appointments, assigned clients, completed work history, preferred requests and commission visibility.
A four-step sequence: the business activates the staff member, the staff member signs in with a Magic Link, works through the day's assignments, and tracks completed work and commission.

merchant_audit.alt: The merchant audit overview open on a laptop, showing reviewed activity totals, flagged events and a filterable record list.
A reviewer working through loose receipts, handwritten daily totals and conflicting notes, with markers for a missing invoice, a voided transaction and a figure that does not match.
A four-step sequence: receive read-only access, sign in securely, review the records, and flag what needs attention.
A padlocked shield beside panels for read-only role access, immutable audit logs, tenant isolation, protected sensitive records and Magic Link sign-in.
